name: ai_choose_moves
title: Move choice of the computer fighter

comments.text: Gives a joystick value to each fighter that the computer controls. The value comes from the pose of the other fighter, the distance and a random column. It does nothing in a two-player game. It also does nothing when $af, $b2, $b4, $b5, $ba or $bb has bit 7 set. Demo ($b3 = 1): both fighters. One-player game: only fighter 1.
The opponent number selects one of 8 tables of 32 column numbers at $c8a2.
X = the fighter that the computer looks at. The computer moves the other fighter.
The pose of the watched fighter selects a pointer to a row list at $c9da.
Distance band 0-7 from $c9b2 selects a row number.
Row address = $cb38 + 8 * row number. A row holds 8 joystick values.
Pointer to the 9 joystick directions at $cdf0 for the move look-up.
X = the fighter that the computer moves.
The counter increments one time for each fighter in each frame.
Demo only: the random number is CIA 1 timer B low EOR timer A low.
Column 0-7 from the level table at a random position 0-31.
Uses the joystick value as input of the computer fighter.
Multiplies A by 8. Output: low byte in A, high byte in $88, carry clear for A < $20.
